Explain why the lecture replaces \\(\\epsilon\\) by \\(\\epsilon/(b-a)\\) at a key step, and show how this choice forces \\(\\left|\\int_a^b f_n-\\int_a^b f\\right|<\\epsilon\\) for all \\(n\\ge m\\) using the triangle inequality for integrals.
answer:
Because integrating a uniform bound \(|f_n-f|<\delta\) over \([a,b]\) yields \(\int_a^b |f_n-f|\le \int_a^b \delta = \delta(b-a)\). To make the final bound equal to \(\epsilon\), the lecture chooses \(\delta=\epsilon/(b-a)\). Then for \(n\ge m\),
\[
\left|\int_a^b f_n-\int_a^b f\right|=\left|\int_a^b (f_n-f)\right|\le \int_a^b |f_n-f|\le \int_a^b \frac{\epsilon}{b-a}=\epsilon.
\]
The key tools are linearity (to write the difference as an integral of a difference) and the triangle inequality for integrals (to move the absolute value inside as an inequality).

answer:
Because \(\sum m_j\) converges, for any \(\epsilon>0\) there exists \(N\) such that the tail \(\sum_{j=N+1}^\infty m_j<\epsilon\). For any \(n\ge N\) and any \(x\),
\[
|f(x)-S_n(x)|=\left|\sum_{j=n+1}^\infty f_j(x)\right|\le \sum_{j=n+1}^\infty |f_j(x)|\le \sum_{j=n+1}^\infty m_j\le \sum_{j=N+1}^\infty m_j<\epsilon.
\]
The same \(N\) works for all \(x\), so the convergence is uniform. Since each \(S_n\) is a finite sum of continuous functions, each \(S_n\) is continuous; by the uniform limit theorem (uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous), \(f\) is continuous.

answer: Uniform convergence has the form: for all \\(\\epsilon>0\\) there exists \(N\) such that for all \(x\) (in the set), the inequality \\(|f_n(x)-f(x)|<\\epsilon\\) holds for all \(n\\ge N\\). The comparison-test tail estimate produces exactly this structure because \(N\) is chosen from the tail \\(\\sum_{j=N+1}^\\infty m_j<\\epsilon\\), which depends only on the numerical series \\(\\sum m_j\\), not on \(x\). That is why the bound \\(|f(x)-S_n(x)|\\le \\sum_{j=N+1}^\\infty m_j\\) holds uniformly in \(x\). Having uniform convergence of the continuous partial sums \(S_n\) to \(f\) is precisely the hypothesis needed to invoke the uniform limit theorem and conclude \(f\) is continuous.
